conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: TradingRangeDayAvoidBuyingNearTopSellingNearBottom
candidates.quote: if it is a trading range day, don't look to buy after a strong bull trend bar or a high 1 near the top of the range, and don't look to short after a strong bear trend bar or low 1 near the bottom of the range.
candidates.description: On a trading-range day, block long entries (even a strong-looking bull trend bar or high-1 setup) when price is near the top of the day's range, and block short entries near the bottom of the range -- range logic favors selling high and buying low, not chasing toward the extremes.

complexity.reason: depends on a trading-range-day classification (a research-grade concept elsewhere in this corpus) plus the day's high/low; the range-position ratio itself is trivial once those exist

notes: This chapter is a list of 78 mostly psychological/discipline/money-management guidelines; only those with an actual bar-level test are recorded as candidates here. The rest are grouped in `rejected` below rather than itemized 78 times.

candidates.name: TakeProfitOnOpposingReversalSetup
candidates.quote: Any reversal setup is a good reason to take partial or full profits, but the setup has to be strong if you are considering a countertrend trade.
candidates.description: Take at least partial profit on an open position whenever a valid reversal setup forms against it, regardless of whether the position itself was entered with-trend or countertrend.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (a discretionary profit-taking trigger keyed to a chart pattern rather than a fixed offset)

complexity.reason: depends on a generic 'valid reversal setup' detector, itself composed from several already-mined reversal-bar/pattern primitives (strong reversal bar, trend-line break, two-bar reversal, etc.)

notes: Generalizes reference/brooks/mined/reversals/21_detailed_day_trading_examples.json's V21-04 (ExitLongOnOpposingLow2SetupUnlessTrendReversed), which is the low-2/high-2-specific instance of this same idea; the dedup pass should decide whether to keep both or fold V21-04 into a placement of this one.

candidates.name: SuddenBreakoutAfterQuietPeriodRequiresConfirmation
candidates.quote: If the market has not given any signals for 30 to 60 minutes... and suddenly the market makes a large bull trend bar that breaks out of a trading range, wait.
candidates.description: If the market has been quiet (no trend-bar/signal activity) for an extended period and then suddenly prints an unusually large trend bar breaking out of the recent tight range, do not enter directly on that bar; require a confirming pullback first.
candidates.pseudocode: quietBarsCount(smallRangeThreshold, lookback) >= minQuietBars && (high[0] - low[0]) >= breakoutBarMultiple * averageRange(lookback) -> defer the entry, require a pullback confirmation instead of the immediate stop entry
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (a confirmation-delay filter on an otherwise-valid breakout entry)

complexity.reason: rolling quiet-period detection plus a size-relative-to-recent-average test on the breakout bar; no cross-bar counters beyond a moving window are needed

notes: The book gives no exact bar count for '30 to 60 minutes'; minQuietMinutes is a reading of the low end.

candidates.name: MoveStopToBreakevenAfterPartialProfitTaken
candidates.quote: Take some or all off on a limit order at a profit target around the prior extreme of the trend, and then move the protective stop to breakeven on any remaining contracts.
candidates.description: After a partial profit exit near a swing/measured-move target, move the protective stop on the remaining position to the original entry price (breakeven).
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (a stop-management rule triggered by a prior partial exit, not a price offset)

complexity.reason: needs a persistent flag for whether a partial exit already occurred on this position, plus the position's own entry price

notes: Overlaps with reference/brooks/mined/reversals/02_signs_of_strength_in_a_reversal.json's BreakevenStop and 01-part_i_trend_reversals....json's BreakevenStopAfterMomentumConfirmation; this candidate's trigger is specifically 'after a partial profit exit', which may be a different condition from those two -- the dedup pass should compare all three.

candidates.name: TradingRangeFadeAfterMultiBarMove
candidates.quote: it is better to only look to short if you are uncertain and the market is up for five to 10 bars, and only look for longs when it is down for five to 10 bars.
candidates.description: In an uncertain (trading-range) market, only permit fade-style short entries after price has moved up for roughly 5 to 10 consecutive bars, and only permit fade-style long entries after it has moved down for roughly 5 to 10 consecutive bars.
candidates.pseudocode: isTradingRange && consecutiveBarsMovingUp(0, lookback) >= minBarsMoved -> permit short-side fade entries
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (an entry-permission gate for countertrend fade setups)

complexity.reason: needs a trading-range classification (research-grade) plus a persistence counter for directional bar movement

candidates.name: FlatEmaTightRangeBarbwireAvoidance
candidates.quote: Beginners should avoid trading in the middle of the day when the market is in the middle of a day's range, especially if the moving average is relatively flat and the trading range is tight and has prominent tails (barbwire).
candidates.description: Avoid entering trades when the moving average is relatively flat, the recent range is tight, and the bars have prominent tails (a 'barbwire' condition), especially around midday.
candidates.pseudocode: isMidDay(0) && abs(ema[0] - ema[emaLookback]) <= flatEmaThreshold && (highest(high, rangeLookback) - lowest(low, rangeLookback)) <= tightRangeThreshold && avgTailFraction(rangeLookback) >= tailFractionThreshold -> block entries

complexity.reason: composite of an EMA-slope test, a range-width test, and an average-tail-length test, each needing an instrument-specific threshold; not a single computation

notes: All numeric thresholds are inventions; the book only gives the qualitative description ('relatively flat', 'tight', 'prominent tails').

Overlaps with reference/brooks/mined/reversals/11_key_times_of_the_day.json's MidDayLowProbabilityWindowFilter; this candidate adds the explicit flat-EMA + barbwire composite test on top of a time-of-day gate, so the dedup pass should compare rather than assume duplication.

candidates.name: AvoidDojiAsSignalBar
candidates.quote: The best signal bars are trend bars in the direction of your trade. Doji bars are one-bar trading ranges and therefore usually terrible signal bars.
candidates.description: Do not use a doji bar as the signal bar for an entry; require the signal bar to be a trend bar in the trade's direction instead.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (a signal-bar quality gate applied wherever a setup's signal bar is tested)

complexity.reason: a negation of an already-defined doji-bar classification

notes: Composes with the DojiBar primitive already defined in reference/brooks/mined/reversals/00_front_matter.json; this candidate is that primitive negated and applied as a signal-bar quality filter rather than redefining doji itself.

candidates.name: BlockReversalEntriesAfterLosingMonth
candidates.quote: If you lost money last month, do not trade any reversals.
candidates.description: If the account's net profit over the prior calendar month was negative, block reversal (countertrend) entries for the current month.
candidates.pseudocode: monthlyNetProfit(priorMonth) < 0 -> block reversal-type entries this month

complexity.reason: requires tracking net profit over the prior completed calendar month, a variant of the trailing-equity read rules/CATALOG.md's MonthlyProfitTarget already performs (there, on the current month's running total instead)

notes: Distinct from MonthlyProfitTarget (a Switch that blocks all entries once the current month's gain hits a target): this reads the PRIOR month's result and only blocks a specific class of entry (reversals), not all trading.

candidates.name: SevenOfTenBarsAboveEmaBlocksShorts
candidates.quote: If seven of the past 10 bars are mostly above the moving average, do not look to short. Instead, only look to buy. If seven of the past 10 bars are mostly below the moving average, do not look to buy. Instead, only look to short.
candidates.description: Block short entries when at least 7 of the last 10 bars closed above the moving average (only longs are permitted); block long entries when at least 7 of the last 10 bars closed below the moving average (only shorts are permitted).
candidates.pseudocode: countIf(close[i] > ema[i], i, 0, lookback - 1) >= minBarsAboveEma -> block short entries

complexity.reason: a rolling count of bars closing above/below their own EMA value over a fixed window; the EMA itself is a standard indicator, and the counting is a simple loop

rejected.quote: Whenever you are positive that your setup is good, don't take the trade. You are missing something.
rejected.reason: pure discretion / trading philosophy on edge size, humility, and the trader's equation, with no bar-level test (guidelines 1-15, plus 31's exit-and-reverse philosophy)

rejected.quote: If you find that you did not take a couple of Emini trades in a row and they worked, you are likely trading too large a position size.
rejected.reason: trading psychology and position-sizing discretion, no bar-level test (guidelines 18-25, 27-29); guideline 24's 'always have a protective stop' is a blanket practice already satisfied by every placement's stop rule, not a new condition

rejected.quote: unless you are a consistently profitable trader, never trade countertrend unless there first has been a strong break of a significant trend line, and the signal is a reasonable setup for an always-in reversal.
rejected.reason: reiterates concepts already captured as primitives elsewhere in this book (trend/trading-range persistence bias, trend-line-break-required-for-reversal, failed-failure resumption, two-legged-move counting, always-in bias, with-trend pullback entries, first-hour timing in 11_key_times_of_the_day.json) without adding new numeric detail (guidelines 17, 30, 32, 34, 35, 36-37, 44-45, 47, 52-54, 56-59, 61-62, 67-69, 71-72)

rejected.quote: Those who talk don't know and those who know don't talk. Don't watch TV or read any news.
rejected.reason: requires news/media/economic-calendar data the engine does not have (guideline 26, and guideline 66's 'not to trade during a report')

rejected.quote: You don't have to trade. You goal as a trader is to make money, not to make trades, so take a trade only when it will help you achieve your goal.
rejected.reason: money-management, personal trading-style, and discipline guidance with no bar-level test (guidelines 27, 39-41, 43, 49-50, 60, 63-65, 68, 70, 74-78)

rejected.quote: Good fill, bad trade. Always be suspicious if the market lets you in or out at a price that is better than you anticipated.
rejected.reason: no fixed, objective threshold for a fill being 'better than anticipated' relative to a trader's own expectation; too subjective to mechanize as a bar-level test (guideline 48)

chapter_summary: Chapter 25 is 78 numbered trading guidelines, and the great majority are trading psychology, discipline, position-sizing, and philosophy of the game (edge size, humility, fear/greed, media avoidance, personal trading style) with no bar-level test; those are grouped into six consolidated rejected entries rather than itemized 78 times. A smaller set of guidelines do carry a concrete, mechanizable condition and are recorded as candidates: avoiding with-trend-looking entries near the wrong end of a trading-range day, taking profit on any opposing reversal setup, requiring confirmation after a sudden breakout following a quiet period, moving the stop to breakeven after a partial profit exit, fading only after a multi-bar directional run in an uncertain market, a flat-EMA/tight-range/barbwire avoidance filter, rejecting doji bars as signal bars, blocking reversal entries after a losing month, and a seven-of-ten-bars-vs-EMA directional bias filter. Several rejected guidelines duplicate primitives already mined in earlier chapters of this book (trend-line-break-required-for-reversal, failed-failure resumption, always-in bias, two-legged-move counting, first-hour timing).
